chapter_theme: The way of restraining the five senses (ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் முறைமை): the senses are fish, elephants and gnawing thieves, and the fort of knowledge alone does not hold them; yet Tirumular mocks those who only cry 'curb the five', since full suppression leaves one inert. What works is letting the senses subside as the mind settles on Nandi, is drawn in by worship and song, and is caught by the Lord's grace.
structure_note: Images of the senses caught or escaping (2031, 2034), a sharp turn against bare suppression (2033) set beside praise of subsiding in the five (2035), the mind as seed of all (2036), and then means: grace, meditation on Nandi, worship and song (2038 to 2043).

2031.reading: In a round pool a cubit deep, holding half a cubit of water, the many fish that lived there have been caught; the fisherman brought his gear and cast it, and now we are free of harm.
2031.nuance: The verse names no meaning for its image. Placed here, the pool is usually taken as the body or the heart, the fish as the senses or desires, and the fisherman (பரவன்) as the Lord or the guru who catches them. The measures (ஒருமுழம், அரைமுழம்) may be symbolic and I can't fix them.

2032.reading: He who sets about curbing the restless senses of this lying body is himself immortal; the mind that goes to the flesh for pleasure runs only as far as it is let run.
2032.nuance: விடக்கு is flesh; விடக்கிண்டு is unclear and may be corrupt. The last line (நடக்கின் நடக்கும் நடக்கும் அளவே) can also mean that the mind goes wherever it is allowed to go, so the curbing lies in not allowing it.

2033.reading: The ignorant say 'curb all five, curb them'; even among the immortals none has curbed all five; knowing that to curb all five is to become inert, I learned the knowledge that does not curb them.
2033.nuance: அசேதனம் is the insentient: a mind with all five senses shut down is no better than matter. The verse is commonly taken as rejecting forced suppression, not restraint itself, since the same chapter praises the senses subsiding (2035) and the senses caught by grace (2031). The word அடக்கு is the one the Kural uses for self-restraint.

2034.reading: Elephants in triple rut rise trumpeting; I built a fort called knowledge to hold them, but they broke out and ran, rushed into great ruin, and that is how the fattened elephants wreck everything.
2034.nuance: The elephants are usually taken as the senses, as in 977; மும்மதம், rut flowing from three places, is sometimes read as the three malas. The point is that knowledge by itself, as a wall, does not hold them.

2035.reading: If one subsides within the five, that is the wide world; if one subsides within the five, that is rare tapas; if one subsides within the five, that is Hara's state; those who subside within the five are the ones who have grace.
2035.nuance: ஒடுங்குதல் is to draw in or subside, not to beat down (அடக்குதல்), and the chapter seems to set the one against the other. ஐந்தில் ஒடுங்கில் can mean the senses settling within their five, or the self drawing back from them. அகலிடம் (the wide place) may be the world or the vast inner space.

2036.reading: What use in babbling at length, what use in thinking of a mirage? The mind is the seed of everything that spreads out; enlarge it and it grows, shrink it and it shrinks; for those who examine, that is all the meaning there is.
2036.nuance: பேய்த்தேர், literally the demon's chariot, is the ordinary word for a mirage. The verse makes the mind, not the senses, the root: whatever world one lives in grows or shrinks with it.

2037.reading: The Lord of unfailing fame, who knows how life wanes and is one with the kin in whom he set the sweet life, makes the five's dancing subside; the serpent that has slain its bonds takes the opening and rests in that path.
2037.nuance: The syntax is loose and the reading is a guess. நாகம் (serpent) and துளை (hole, opening) may be kundalini entering the central channel, as yogic readings take it, with அஞ்சாடல் ஒடுக்க as the stilling of the five senses' play.

2038.reading: Tie the five elements that leapt about to the post of knowledge where the spreading light rests; if grace grants what is called bliss, that becomes the higher destiny that covers one over.
2038.nuance: பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும் are the five elements, here probably standing for the senses built from them, tied like cattle to a post (தறி). வேய்ந்துகொள் (to roof, to cover) and மேலை விதி (the higher rule or fate) are unclear.

2039.reading: If you think daily on Nandi who moves within, gently drawing in the spreading thought, and the mind fixed on its mark looks along the mark's path, north and south become the temple of the mind.
2039.nuance: பைய (gently) again sets drawing in against forcing. குறி (mark, sign) is a yogic term for the point of concentration. வடக்கொடு தெற்கு may mean the whole world or, in the body, the line from crown to base; either way the shrine is the mind.

2040.reading: Some many nazhigais and days have gone; the wealth that seemed lasting is like writing on water; conquer the senses and let them go at once, and even if a mountain falls you can bear it.
2040.nuance: நீள்பொருள் may be lasting wealth or the long-lived body. விடுமின்கள் can mean 'let the senses go' or 'free yourselves'. The last line promises steadiness, not escape: the mountain still falls.

2041.reading: Praise and sing the holy form of the Pure One and worship it; then, turning back the five senses with the intellect, pour into the heart the Lord of the four directions and of all who come after, and gathering into one becomes possible.
2041.nuance: The order is worship first, then the senses turned back by புத்தி (intellect), then the Lord poured (ஊற்றுக) into the heart. ஒருங்கல் is the mind gathered into one.

2042.reading: No one perceives the five who gnaw within the embodied state where the heart is held; if one speaks of many things as if in jest, it becomes a mountain wrapped in streaked darkness.
2042.nuance: சகளம் is the state with form, the embodied soul or the Lord in form. The second half is obscure: மைசூழ் வரை, a mountain surrounded by black, may be delusion piling up from idle talk.

2043.reading: There is nothing one must give up; reaching him in your thought, praise him with song; the senses that arose from the craving of the five false ones are only five.
2043.nuance: The first line seems to answer the call to renounce: nothing needs abandoning if the Lord is held within and sung. The last two lines are unclear; ஐந்தே may belittle the senses (they are only five) once their root, craving, is seen.

links.note: The Kural says the field of the five must be crushed (அடல்வேண்டும்); Tirumular calls those who say 'curb the five' ignorant and says full curbing makes one inert. The conflict holds if 2033 is read as rejecting suppression of the senses, as its wording says, rather than only a wrong method of it.
The same chapter that mocks curbing the five (அடக்கு) praises subsiding in the five (ஒடுங்கு) as tapas and Hara's state: the objection is to forcing the senses, not to their stilling.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be held, the Kural's guarded by the goad of firmness (on Parimelazhagar's reading), Tirumular's by a fort of knowledge. In the Kural the guard works; in Tirumular the elephants break out.
In 977 the five elephants of the forest are held by the goad of the five letters; in 2034 a fort of knowledge fails to hold them. Mantra succeeds where bare knowledge did not.
Both make mastery of the five a supreme power: the Kural calls Indra witness to it, Tirumular calls it the wide world, tapas and Hara's state.
Both count life away by its units of time, the Kural's day a saw cutting life, Tirumular's nazhigais and days already gone; Tirumular draws the lesson of conquering the senses now.

2032 says he who sets about curbing the restless senses (இந்திரியம் அடக்கல்) is himself immortal (அமரன்); Kural 6 says those who keep the path of the one who quenched the five sense-doors (பொறிவாயில் ஐந்தவித்தான்) live long (நீடுவாழ்வார்). Both promise lasting life for sense-restraint; the Kural gives it to those who follow the restrained one, the Tirumanthiram to the one who restrains.

2036 asks what use babbling (பிதற்றில்) is and says the mind is the seed of all that spreads, growing or shrinking with it; 2956 says the mind's maya is maya, when it dies nothing else remains, there is no need to babble (பிதற்றவும் வேண்டா), and to remain having examined oneself is the truth. Both make the mind the root of the world one lives in and examination (ஆராய்ந்து / ஆய்ந்து) the answer.

2038 bids one tie the leaping five to the post of knowledge (ஞானத் தறி); 2023 says the five rutting elephants of the body will not come to the post of the Agamas (ஆகமத் தறி) and the mahout is spent. The same tethering post, failing in 2023 when it is scripture, holding in 2038 when it is knowledge and grace grants bliss.

2040 says the wealth that seemed lasting (நீள்பொருள்) is like writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்து), so conquer the senses now; 64 says crores of Agamas are writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்தே) if one does not know the knowledge the Lord declared. The same figure strikes wealth in one and unread scripture in the other: both are void without the inner work.

2041 begins 'போற்றிசைத்துப் புனிதன்', worships the Lord of the four directions (நாற்றிசைக்கும் நாதனை), then turns the senses back and pours him into the heart; 2, the book's opening praise, has 'போற்றிசைத்து ... புனிதனை' and 'நாற்றிசைக்கும் ... நாதனை'. 2041 reuses the invocation's words and makes the praise the first step of sense-withdrawal.

2043 says 'கைவிடலாவது ஒன்று இல்லை', there is nothing one must give up, if one reaches him in thought and sings; Kural 341 says from whatever one has left, from that one has no pain, making release from pain follow each thing renounced. On the reading that 2043 answers the call to renounce objects, the two disagree on whether giving things up is the way; if 2043 means only that renunciation is secondary to praise, they differ in emphasis.

source_issues: 2032 line 3: விடக்கிண்டு is obscure and may be corrupt.
2037 and 2042: the syntax is loose and the second halves are obscure; the text may be damaged.
